_readme: What retailers are EXPECTED to have this week, in store and online.
Drives /drops.html. Updated weekly by hand from a restock community's
week-ahead post.
THIS IS THE ONLY PAGE ON THE SITE MADE OF FORECASTS RATHER THAN FACTS, and
the whole design follows from that. Everywhere else the rule is that a
number is traceable to a source. Here nothing is: no retailer announces its
restock schedule, and the community reporting it is reading shelves, backend
listings and each other. So the page does not pretend. Every row carries a
confidence, the page says in its lede that none of this is announced by
anyone, and it prints the date it was compiled at the top rather than
burying it.
NOT OUR FINDINGS, AND THE PAGE HAS TO SAY SO IN THOSE WORDS. Everything
here was read somewhere else and passed on. The site's credibility
everywhere else is that its numbers are sourced; this page's honesty is that
its forecasts are flagged as somebody else's forecasts. `source` at the top
of this file is printed in the lede AND again at the foot of every single
card, because a card is the unit somebody screenshots and a page-level
credit does not travel with it.
KEEP THE HEDGES THAT CAME WITH THE CLAIM. The posts these rows come from are
written in hedges: 'expect to see', 'may see', 'nothing confirmed', 'based on
recent patterns', 'select stores', 'we don't know what products it will be'.
Copy them across. Turning 'expected Tuesday 3am based on recent patterns'
into 'drops Tuesday 3am' is the single easiest way to make this page lie, and
it reads as tidying up.
STALENESS IS THE FAILURE MODE. A restock page showing last week is worse
than no restock page, because it sends somebody to a shop for nothing. The
builder compares `weekOf` against the newest video in the catalogue, the
same clock /upcoming.html uses, and when the week has passed the page says
so at the top instead of presenting stale rows as current. It does not hide
them: last week's expectations are still useful for reading a pattern.
AND SOME ROWS DIE BEFORE THE WEEK DOES, WHICH IS THE SECOND MECHANISM.
`expires` is the last day a row can possibly be true, as a plain ISO date,
and it defaults to `weekEnds` when it is absent. A row whose `expires` is
EARLIER than `weekEnds` is PERISHABLE: it is a single afternoon or a single
evening rather than a week's worth of shelf watching, so once its day has
gone it is not a record of anything, it is just wrong. Those rows are
dropped by the builder when the build clock is past them and swept out of
the page again by the reader's own clock, the same belt-and-braces shape
scripts/build-shows.mjs uses on past card shows. A perishable row also SAYS
on its own face which day it covers and that it comes off the page after
that, so nobody has to trust the sweep to know what they are reading.
The two mechanisms do different jobs and neither replaces the other. The
week banner covers 'nobody has touched this site in a month'. The per-row
sweep covers 'it is Wednesday and Monday's one-afternoon alert is still
sitting there looking current'. Do not add a third.
`window` is optional and is {from, to} in ISO dates, for a row that names a
specific day or range. It is stamped onto the card as data attributes so the
claim is machine readable, and it does NOT drive expiry: a product loaded on
a backend with an expected Tuesday can still turn up on the Friday, so the
row outlives the day the trackers guessed.
CONFIDENCE, and it uses the same three words as data/upcoming.json so the
two pages mean the same thing by them:
confirmed  a date the retailer itself has put on something, or stock
already confirmed sitting on shelves
window     expected within a known range, e.g. a usual drop day and hour
expected   the community thinks it is coming and has no date
pattern    a recurring day or time people have noticed. THE WEAKEST TIER
and it needs its own word, because no retailer on earth
publishes a Pokemon restock schedule. 'Walmart Wednesday' is
folklore that happens to be well observed, not a timetable.
A row here should carry a source for the observation or say
plainly that it is a pattern nobody has measured.
A ROW BUILT ON WATCHING A BACKEND IS `pattern`, NOT `window`. Backend
movement on a retailer's site is an observation by somebody outside the
company, so it has no official origin, and `window` and `expected` both
imply one because that is what they mean on /upcoming.html. This caught the
two Pokemon Center rows for the week of August 17, 2026: both were tempting to
file as `window` because both name an hour.
CHANNEL is `store` or `online`. Several retailers do both and they are
separate rows, because the answer to when and how you get it is different.
RETAILER IDENTITY, and this changed on 2026-08-15 after the reasoning was
actually checked. The name is drawn in the site's own typeface. There is no
logo and no brand color, and the second half of that is the part that took
research to get right.
Each retailer used to carry a `tint` holding its brand color. Two things
killed it. First, it did not work: Walgreens and Family Dollar shipped 1.6
just-noticeable-differences apart, which no eye separates, and it does not
improve with better sourcing because Target and Costco both use Pantone 186,
an exact match. US big-box retail is red and blue almost to a shop. Colour
cannot identify a retailer here, so the NAME has to, and it does.
Second, six of the ten colors had no published source. Every retailer
checked either says nothing or requires written consent for logo use, and
the trackers that do show logos are affiliates with a contract. A solid
white-on-brand-color chip is also the most endorsement-suggestive form
there is, on the one page that must not look retailer-sanctioned.
So `kind` now carries the color instead, from the site's own palette. It
groups the page the way a reader actually scans it, it is the site's own
categorisation rather than a claim about somebody's brand, and it needs no
sourcing because it asserts nothing about anyone.
SOURCE. `source` names where the week's post came from and when it was
read. If a week's information comes from somewhere else, change it: the page
prints whatever is here, so it can never credit the wrong place.
NAME THE KIND OF PLACE, NOT THE PLACE. These posts come out of stock
tracking communities, several of which are private or paid. Do not put a
community's name, its channel names or an invite link in here. 'Community
restock trackers' plus the date it was read is the whole of what this page
can honestly say and the whole of what a reader needs: the credit is that
these are not our findings, and no reader is served by being pointed at a
server they cannot join. Same call /decks.html makes about Limitless, for
the same reason, and it is written up in CLAUDE.md under the outbound rule.
`url` stays null. A row may still name a PUBLISHED, PUBLIC measurement in
its note text, with the date it was read, because that is a number and a
number has to be traceable.
WHY THIS IS PASTED IN BY HAND AND ALWAYS WILL BE. Every retailer surface
that would carry drop information was probed on 2026-08-15 and is either
bot-blocked or robots-disallowed: Pokemon Center disallows the exact
availability endpoints, Target's store-availability API answers 403 to
datacenter IPs, GameStop 403s even its robots.txt, and Walgreens and
pokemon.com serve challenge pages that look like 200s. The community
trackers that do hold the data publish rendered pages with no feed, no API
and no reuse licence.
The Pokemon Company's own monthly release article names ONE retailer,
Pokemon Center, and calls everywhere else 'where other Pokemon TCG products
are sold', so even the official calendar does not identify retailer
exclusives.
None of that is the real reason though. The real reason is that this
information does not exist in machine-readable form because it does not
exist in advance at all. Nobody knows, including the retailers.

source.name: Community restock trackers
source.note: Stock tracking communities the owner follows, passed on as they were written. Not an announcement from any retailer, and not this site's own findings.

drops.what: Be on alert for a Pokemon Center drop this week. The trackers say we are in the official window where 30th Celebration Ultra Premium Collections and Delta Reign preorders can go live, and that they will pass on any indication of a drop ahead of time.
drops.when: The most common drop days are Monday to Wednesday, 11am to 2pm Eastern.

drops.what: Ascended Heroes Elite Trainer Boxes are starting to wrap up at Costco. Ascended Heroes Mini Tins, both the 5-pack and the 10-pack, are starting to stock in store at select locations instead.
drops.when: Store by store, through the week. The trackers say they will post a list each day of which warehouses have stock, and run more than one check a day.

drops.what: The trackers expect an online drop for the Ascended Heroes Mini Tins as well, sometime this week.
drops.when: No day given, just this week.

drops.what: Destined Rivals Elite Trainer Boxes will continue to stock in store at select locations, alongside Ascended Heroes Large Tins.
drops.when: No day given. Select locations, through the week.
notes: The trackers say their own tooling will tell you how many units each Best Buy near you is holding if you give it a zip code, so you can plan which shop to try. That is their measurement rather than ours and we have not checked it.
They add that they will be watching through the week for other high demand items and updating stock counts as they go.

drops.what: A SECOND WAVE of 30th Celebration products is expected to release in store on Sunday, September 27. Alongside it, expect the usual restocks of Ascended Heroes Large Tins, Chaos Rising, Pitch Black and First Partner product, plus any 30th Celebration stock left over from the first release.
drops.when: Sunday, September 27 for the second wave, which is the trackers' expectation and not a date Target has published. The rest is store by store through the week.

drops.what: If your store did not get 30th Celebration product last week for the release, expect it to arrive this week.
drops.when: The trackers report that Walmart's internal communications have the remaining stores RECEIVING product on Tuesday, September 22 and putting it out during a window of September 23 to 25. That is a claim about a retailer's internal messaging, passed on as it was written, and Walmart has published nothing.

drops.what: Select clubs are continuing to randomly restock their second wave of Ascended Heroes Focused Fighters in store.
drops.when: No day, and the trackers are explicit about why: having it on hand does not mean a club will put it out that day. It is each individual store's decision when to stock it.
notes: The trackers keep an updated list of which clubs currently have stock on the shelf.

drops.what: No products are loaded on the back end of Target at the moment. The trackers expect that to change as the week progresses, and say they will post the products once they load, ahead of time.

Select stores are still receiving Black Bolt and White Flare Unova Poster Collections, and select stores are still stocking 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Boxes, Poster Collections and Tech Sticker Collections.
drops.when: No day given, store by store.

drops.what: Nothing is loaded on Walmart for an online raffle or for the usual Walmart Wednesday yet. The trackers are still expecting the usual weekly Walmart restock and say they will pass on any change.
drops.when: Walmart Wednesday is a pattern people have noticed rather than a timetable Walmart publishes.
